notes.reason: The speaker here is the guest, Sarah Paine, a professor at the Naval War College, and she does assert that the two Koreas show what sanctions do to growth over several generations, so the claim is genuinely made in the video even though it is not Dwarkesh's own. The note fails on its own facts. It says the divergence happened 'decades before comprehensive UN sanctions began in 2006', but the United States imposed a total trade embargo on North Korea on 30 June 1950 under the Trading with the Enemy Act and the export control laws, and that embargo stayed in force until 2000 and was only formally lifted in 2008. So North Korea was cut off from the Western trading order through exactly the 1970s and 1980s the note points at, and the note's own source says North Korea's isolation 'prevented access to advanced foreign technology'. Paine's whole argument in this clip is about being shut out of the maritime trading order, which is the same mechanism, so the note sets up a false choice between 'domestic economic choices' and 'sanctions' when the standard account involves both. A historian of exactly this subject would read the note as a factual error about when North Korea was first embargoed, and answering her with it would embarrass us.
